title: The Ten Foundational Axioms of Constitutional Capitalism
purpose: Distill a conceptually rich philosophy into a coherent operating doctrine. Every principle, policy, and constitutional proposal should be traceable to one or more axioms. This is philosophy integration — not another policy domain and not a new CC-PRIN-* ID.

foundational_philosophy_diagnosis.layer_percent_note: Progress snapshots currently report Foundational Philosophy around 82% (capped). That remaining share is not a call for more domain ideas — it is a call to integrate, bound, and operationalize the philosophy already built.
remaining_work_is: traceability from applications back to axioms

derivation_rule.text: If a doctrine item cannot be derived from the First Principle and one or more Foundational Axioms, it should be questioned — and routed to the Architecture Incubator rather than treated as settled philosophy.
derivation_rule.freeze_compliance: No new principle ID. Axioms organize existing philosophy under CC-DEC-093/094 discipline.

first_principle.title: First Principle
first_principle.text: The purpose of a free society is to maximize the ability of every person and every community to build, share, and sustain prosperity through liberty, responsibility, opportunity, and voluntary cooperation.

related_existing.text: The purpose of an economy is not merely to create wealth, but to create a prosperous, free, and self-governing people.
The people are the nation's greatest source of productive capacity, creativity, innovation, and self-government.
Power should always flow toward the people, never permanently away from them.

first_principle.rule: Everything else — education, healthcare, retirement, farming, local ownership, civic service — should be traceable back to this First Principle. Existing Declaration and civilizational texts are not rewritten by this distillation; they are organized under it.

axioms.title: Definition of Prosperity
axioms.text: Prosperity is the durable capacity of persons and communities to live with financial security, health of body and mind, strong families, educational opportunity, community trust, property and enterprise ownership, civic participation, environmental stewardship, freedom and dignity, and generational mobility.
axioms.why: Without a formal definition, later policies risk pulling in different directions.

axioms.title: Role of Government
axioms.text: Government exists to establish the rules, infrastructure, and institutions that allow free people and free communities to flourish while protecting liberty, justice, and fair competition.
axioms.why: Provides a consistent lens for evaluating proposals without ideology of size alone.

axioms.title: Role of Markets
axioms.text: Competitive markets are the preferred mechanism for allocating most goods and services, provided they operate under transparent rules, protect competition, and do not permit the concentration of power that undermines liberty or equal opportunity.
axioms.framing: Markets are neither inherently virtuous nor inherently harmful. They are tools.
axioms.why: Connects market preference to constitutional principles rather than ideology.

axioms.title: Theory of Ownership
axioms.text: Ownership — personal, family, employee, cooperative, community, and public where appropriate — creates responsibility, accountability, and long-term investment in the success of people and places.
axioms.why: Unifies farms, cooperatives, community investment, and retirement under one philosophical account of why ownership matters.

axioms.title: Intergenerational Responsibility
axioms.text: Every generation should leave its communities, institutions, natural resources, and public finances stronger than it inherited them.

axioms.title: Philosophy of Community
axioms.text: Communities are the primary institutions through which people develop trust, relationships, mutual aid, identity, and shared prosperity.

axioms.title: Liberty and Shared Responsibility
axioms.text: Liberty is essential; responsibility gives liberty meaning; communities thrive when people voluntarily contribute to institutions that benefit everyone.

balance.voluntary_contribution: encouraged without making civic service or local investment compulsory

axioms.title: Philosophy of Human Capital
axioms.text: People are the nation's greatest productive asset. Investment in people is not consumption; it is productive capital formation.
axioms.dignity_guardrail: A person is never merely a resource. People are citizens with inherent dignity and rights.

axioms.title: Ethical Guardrails
axioms.text: Constitutional Capitalism will not compromise equal dignity, the rule of law, due process, freedom of speech and conscience, private property, democratic accountability, transparency, anti-corruption, or competition over favoritism.
axioms.why: These are not policies — they are guardrails that constrain every future proposal.

axioms.title: Traceability and Operational Coherence
axioms.text: Applications of Constitutional Capitalism — education, healthcare, energy, retirement, farming, ownership, resilience — must remain derivable from the First Principle and Axioms 1–9. Philosophy becomes simpler and more coherent by distillation, not by adding domains.
axioms.why: Makes the remaining foundational-philosophy work about integration rather than expansion.

component_maturity_estimate.note: Honest working estimates of distillation maturity — not Phase 2 proof scores and not a claim that Foundational Philosophy is finished.
component_maturity_estimate.synthesis: Conceptually rich but not yet fully distilled into a coherent operating doctrine.

declaration_rule.text: Do not silently rewrite the Declaration. Axioms organize and bound philosophy for operational use; any Declaration amendment requires explicit Steve approval.
